avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inducer may reduce ketamine levels and efficacy; also increases risk of serotonergic effects
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue St. John's Wort at least 2 weeks before ketamine therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Grapefruit Extract/Seed
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor increases ketamine concentrations and risk of adverse effects including dissociation and cardiovascular changes
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid grapefruit products entirely during ketamine treatment

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium
caution_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate NMDA antagonism and enhance dissociative effects; theoretical additive CNS depression
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased dissociation or dizziness; use standard supplemental doses only

caution_supplements.name: Valerian Root
caution_supplements.action: Counsel on possible increased sedation; monitor clinical response

caution_supplements.name: Kava Kava
caution_supplements.mechanism: May enhance CNS depression and dissociative effects
caution_supplements.action: Avoid or use with caution; counsel on increased risk of sedation and dissociation

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases ketamine bioavailability and plasma concentrations, elevating risk of toxicity and adverse effects
avoid_foods.action: Eliminate grapefruit and pomelo from diet during ketamine therapy

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay gastric clearance and absorption if oral ketamine is used; potential for variable bioavailability
caution_foods.action: Take oral ketamine consistently with or without food to maintain steady-state levels

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive CNS depression and increased dissociative/psychotomimetic effects; impairs judgment and coordination
caution_foods.action: Strongly counsel against alcohol use; monitor for excessive sedation or dissociation

monitoring_notes: Monitor for signs of excessive dissociation, altered mental status, and cardiovascular changes (blood pressure, heart rate). Assess for drug-drug interactions at CYP3A4/2B6 level, particularly with inducers or inhibitors, as ketamine has narrow therapeutic margins in clinical settings.
